problem: The ALFRED Seq2Seq baseline navigates poorly (61.9% subgoal success for navigation in the pretrained model) because it must decode very long action sequences, sees only a forward view, and has no language-grounding supervision or goal-direction signal during navigation.
motivation: Navigation precedes almost every manipulation subgoal in ALFRED, so navigation failures cascade into overall failure. The baseline is trained by imitation only, with no exploration and no supervision for grounding landmarks in navigation instructions, so it is hard for it to find the destination.
key_idea: Train per-subgoal, add panoramic views with a YOLOv4 object detector, and use a BERT-based localizer to predict the angle to the goal location at every step as an extra input to the Seq2Seq policy.
insight: An oracle that supplies the ground-truth goal angle raises val-seen navigation subgoal SR from 30.0 to 67.8 and val-unseen from 26.5 to 35.4, so goal-direction tracking is a key navigation bottleneck. The learned localizer captures only a small part of this gap (unseen 28.8 SR vs 26.5). Step-by-step granular training mainly improves action F1 (75.6 to 85.3 on unseen) rather than navigation success.
method: Granular training: the model is trained and run one subgoal at a time with only that subgoal's instruction, which shortens the LSTM decoding sequence.
Panoramic observations: for navigation subgoals, images at 8 rotation angles (45° apart) are collected per timestep; at inference this is done by forcing 8 consecutive rotations.
Object detection: YOLOv4 is trained on robot-view images with AI2-THOR bounding boxes and detects 203 object categories in all views.

Spatial tokens: each box is projected to horizontal angle θ and vertical angle φ in panoramic space and encoded as (sinθ, cosθ, sinφ, w, h), repeated to BERT embedding size and added to the BERT embedding of the class label.

Localizer: multimodal BERT takes [CLS], spatial tokens, [SEP], instructions L_k and L_{k+1}, [SEP]; a linear layer on [CLS] regresses sin/cos of the angle to the goal, and this d_t is appended to the Seq2Seq input (a zero vector is used for non-navigation subgoals).
Oracle variant: the ground-truth d_t is fed directly to give an upper bound for spatial tracking.

setting.backbone: ALFRED Seq2Seq (BiLSTM language encoder, frozen ResNet, LSTM decoder) + BERT localizer + YOLOv4 detector (trained)
setting.training_data: ALFRED demonstrations for only the 'stack and place' task type; extra AI2-THOR panoramic images and bounding boxes for YOLOv4 and the localizer
setting.observation: egocentric RGB plus 8-angle panoramic RGB views, detected bounding boxes with class labels
setting.action_space: low-level primitive navigation actions (move, turn, look) and manipulation actions with predicted binary masks
setting.privileged: none for the localizer model; the oracle variant uses the ground-truth goal angle

numbers_note: Only one task type (stack and place) was used. Full goal success rate was not reported; only goal-condition SR, which is near 0.
results: On the stack-and-place subset, the localizer raises unseen action F1 from 75.6 (baseline) to 88.7 and nav subgoal SR slightly from 27.5 to 28.8. On seen rooms its nav SR falls from 31.0 to 25.4. The oracle reaches 67.8 seen / 35.4 unseen nav SR, well above the learned localizer.
limitations: Evaluated only on the 'stack and place' task type because of training time; goal SR is ~0, so end-to-end gains are not shown.
Learned localizer barely improves navigation success and hurts val-seen (25.4 vs 31.0 baseline).
There is no ablation isolating panoramic views or the object detector, and inference needs 8 extra rotations per step.
